newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway says 1996 oil output exceeded new finds.
newsitem.headline: Norway says 1996 oil output exceeded new finds.

text.p: Norway produced more crude in 1996 than was discovered by exploration drilling, the Oil Directorate said on Wednesday.
It said oil accounted for around 60 percent, or 60 to 115 million cubic metres, of total hydrocarbons discoveries of between 100 and 190 million cubic metres of oil equivalent.
The Scandinavian country pumped 176 million cubic metres of crude in the 12-month period.

The directorate said exploration on the Norwegian continental shelf in 1996 produced 10 new hydrocarbon finds, all of which were in the North Sea. Six of the discoveries were oil finds, one gas and three were gas/condensate shows.
It said none of the discoveries were as large as fields already in production but most were candidates for development due to their proximity to existing or planned infrastructure.
Between 40 and 75 million cubic metres of gas were found in 1996 compared with production of 36 million cubic metres.

The directorate said 1997 would be an exciting year for exploration activity with drilling expected to begin on the first deep water structure in the Norwegian Sea. There also were plans for new spuds in the North Sea and in shallow waters in the Norwegian Sea.
In addition two new wells would be drilled in the Barents Sea after a break in activity of more than three years, it said.
"Drilling activity is expected to stabilise at the 1996 level over the next few years at around 35 exploration wells and 140 production wells per year," the directorate said.
